title: Lotus Temple Delhi - Symbol of Peace, Beauty, and Harmony
content:
Lotus Temple - Delhi, 

The Lotus Temple in Delhi is one of the city’s most iconic landmarks, known for its flower-like design and peaceful environment. Built in 1986, it is a Bahá’í House of Worship, open to people of all religions to meditate, pray, or simply enjoy the calm atmosphere.

The temple is shaped like a blooming white lotus, made of marble and surrounded by nine pools of water and lush gardens. Its unique design symbolizes purity, peace, and harmony, making it one of the most visited attractions in Delhi.

Inside the temple, there are no idols, rituals, or sermons—just silence. Visitors are encouraged to sit quietly, reflect, or meditate, making it a rare spiritual experience in the heart of the bustling city.

Best Time to Visit: The Lotus Temple can be visited throughout the year, but the best time is from October to March when the weather is pleasant. The temple is open from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, and entry is completely free.

How to Reach:

  • By Metro: Nearest station is Kalkaji Mandir (Violet Line), just a short walk away.
  • By Bus/Auto: Well-connected by buses; autos easily available from nearby hubs.
  • By Car: Parking available near the entrance.

Entry Fee: 

Free for all visitors.

Travel Tip: Keep your visit silent inside the prayer hall - this is a space for reflection, and the hush is part of its magic.
